# Concepts & Claims

Every Green Goods concept as a human card — what it is, why it matters, what it must never be confused with — plus the public claim ledger with the evidence behind each claim. Maturity is the five-dimension capability projection (build · deploy · activate · index · in-app). Legend: ✓ complete · ◐ partial · ⛔ blocked · ✗ not started · — not applicable.

## Concept cards

### Garden

**Garden** — The home unit of Green Goods — a real community in a real place, with its own treasury, roles, and record.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ✓ · in-app ✓
- **Definition**: A community of gardeners rooted in a place, represented on-chain as an ERC-721 garden token whose ERC-6551 token-bound account holds the garden's treasury, role Hats, and metadata.
- **Example**: TAS HUB in Awka, Nigeria documents solar and education work as one garden.
- **Also called**: community garden · garden community
- **Not to be confused with Commitment Pool**: a garden may open exactly one commitment pool; the pool is a ledger inside the garden, not the garden itself
- **Related**: has-many → Vault · has-tree → Hat
- **Safe claim**: Gardens are live on Arbitrum One with Season One communities operating today.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/tokens/Garden.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → gardenToken` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → rootGarden.address` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → rootGarden.tokenId` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/indexer/schema.graphql` · `packages/client/src/views/Public/Gardens.tsx`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Action

**Action template** — The menu of documentable work — each action defines what evidence counts before anyone submits.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ✓ · in-app ✓
- **Definition**: A documented activity a gardener can perform — the unit of work template (e.g. "Plant native species", "Remove invasive growth").
- **Example**: “Plant native species” with photo evidence and a species count.
- **Also called**: action template · work template
- **Not to be confused with Work**: an Action is the template; Work is one documented instance of it
- **Related**: enabled-by-domain-mask → Garden
- **Safe claim**: The action registry is live; gardens choose which actions are open for submissions.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/registries/Action.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → actionRegistry` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/indexer/schema.graphql` · `packages/client/src/views/Public/Actions.tsx`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Work

**Documented work** — The atomic unit of proof: field evidence that becomes an on-chain record at submission — or the moment it syncs, when captured offline.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ◐ · in-app ✓
- **Definition**: One documented instance of an Action performed by a gardener — media, notes, and metadata submitted as an EAS Work attestation for operator review; approval records a separate Work Approval attestation.
- **Example**: Twelve seedlings planted, three photos, submitted from an offline queue when signal returned.
- **Also called**: submission · field log
- **Not to be confused with Commitment**: Work documents what happened; a commitment records a promise that work will happen
- **Related**: instance-of → Action · performed-in → Garden
- **Safe claim**: Work is attested on-chain at submission; operator approval adds a separate linked approval record.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/resolvers/Work.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → schemas.workSchemaUID` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → workResolver` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/client/src/views/Garden/index.tsx`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Assessment

**Garden assessment** — The up-front baseline and strategy that frames a season of work before it begins — success criteria first, work second.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ◐ · in-app ✓
- **Definition**: An up-front baseline and strategy for a garden — domain, diagnosis, SMART outcome targets, selected Actions, reporting period — authored by an evaluator or operator before work begins, mirrored to a Karma GAP milestone when that module is active; explicitly not a review of submitted Work (that is Work Approval).
- **Example**: An evaluator sets a waste-domain baseline with three SMART outcomes for the quarter.
- **Also called**: baseline · strategy kernel
- **Not to be confused with Work**: an assessment frames future work; it is explicitly not a review of submitted Work (that is Work Approval)
- **Related**: frames → Garden
- **Safe claim**: Assessments are live; evaluators and operators author them before work begins.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/resolvers/Assessment.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → schemas.assessmentSchemaUID` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → schemas.assessmentV3SchemaUID` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → assessmentResolver` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/admin/src/components/Assessment/CreateAssessmentSteps/StrategyKernelStep.tsx`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Hypercert

**Impact certificate** — Bundles a period of approved work into a fundable certificate, so finished work can attract support.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ◐ · in-app ✓
- **Definition**: An on-chain claim of impact bundling approved Work into a fractional impact certificate. Funders hold fractions; gardeners hold contribution credit.
- **Example**: A season of approved agroforestry work minted as one certificate with contributor shares.
- **Also called**: impact certificate
- **Not to be confused with Attestation**: attestations are the raw records; a hypercert is a curated bundle of them
- **Related**: bundles → Work · minted-for → Garden
- **Safe claim**: Operators mint impact certificates from approved work on Arbitrum today.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/modules/Hypercerts.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → hypercertsModule` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → hypercertMinter` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → marketplaceAdapter` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/admin/src/components/Hypercerts/ActiveListingsTable.tsx`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Vault

**Garden vault** — Lets funders endow a garden: principal stays put while generated yield funds operations.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ✓ · in-app ✓
- **Definition**: The garden's treasury. Funders deposit; the garden's Tokenbound Account holds; yield splits flow to operators / gardeners / community per configured ratios.
- **Example**: A funder deposits into a garden's vault; the garden harvests the yield each period.
- **Also called**: endowment · Octant vault
- **Not to be confused with Cookie Jar**: vaults hold endowment principal; cookie jars hold small operational funds for frequent withdrawals
- **Related**: treasury-of → Garden
- **Safe claim**: Vault deposits, withdrawals, and yield harvests are live on Arbitrum.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/modules/Octant.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → octantModule` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → yieldSplitter` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/client/src/views/Public/Vaults.tsx`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Cookie Jar

**Cookie jar** — Small, rule-bound operational funds — capped withdrawals on an interval, so everyday expenses don't need a treasury vote.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ◐ · in-app ✓
- **Definition**: A garden-scoped emergency or discretionary fund with rate-limited withdrawals. Allowlisted members can claim within the configured cap.
- **Example**: A gardener withdraws the weekly cap to buy seedlings.
- **Also called**: jar
- **Not to be confused with Vault**: jars are for frequent small spending; vaults are for principal that generates yield
- **Related**: discretionary-fund-of → Garden
- **Safe claim**: Garden jars are provisioned automatically at garden mint; jar activity beyond creation is not yet indexed for reports.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/modules/CookieJar.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → cookieJarFactory` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → cookieJarModule` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/admin/src/views/Cookies/index.tsx`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Attestation

**On-chain record** — The permanence layer: every claim in Green Goods resolves to a signed, public, verifiable EAS record.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ◐ · in-app ✓
- **Definition**: An EAS (Ethereum Attestation Service) record. Used for Work submissions, Assessment outcomes, and other off-chain-verifiable claims.
- **Example**: A Work attestation and its linked Work Approval, both inspectable on easscan.
- **Also called**: EAS attestation · record
- **Not to be confused with Hypercert**: a hypercert is a token bundling many attestations
- **Related**: records → Work · records → Assessment
- **Safe claim**: Green Goods registers five EAS schemas on Arbitrum; core records are attested and publicly verifiable.
- **Evidence**: `packages/shared/src/modules/data/eas.ts` · `packages/contracts/config/schemas.json` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → schemas.workSchemaUID` · `packages/indexer/schema.graphql` · `packages/client/src/views/Public/Impact.tsx`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Hat

**Role hat** — Transparent, revocable authority: who may approve, submit, or assess is readable on-chain, not implied.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ✓ · in-app ✓
- **Definition**: A Hats Protocol role token. Determines on-chain authority — operator hats approve Work, gardener hats submit Work, evaluator hats author Assessments. Work review is never the evaluator's job.
- **Example**: An operator hat lets its wearer approve work; revoking the hat removes the authority.
- **Also called**: role · Hats Protocol role
- **Not to be confused with Garden**: hats grant authority within a garden; they are not membership itself
- **Related**: authority-in → Garden
- **Safe claim**: Garden roles are live Hats Protocol tokens; the on-chain operator hat labels already read Steward.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/lib/Hats.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → hatsModule` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/admin/src/views/Community/index.tsx`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Season

**Season** — The shared clock of a garden — a bounded period that frames assessments, work, and harvest.

- **Maturity**: build ✗ · deploy — · active — · indexed — · in-app ◐
- **Definition**: A bounded period (typically a quarter) during which a garden runs a coordinated set of Actions and Assessments. Pacing primitive — never a countdown.
- **Example**: Season One: the current cohort of live gardens documenting work on Arbitrum.
- **Also called**: garden season
- **Not to be confused with Commitment Cycle**: a pool's Season cycle is the planned on-chain form of this same concept — one Season, two representations, not two Seasons
- **Related**: formalized-by → Commitment Cycle
- **Safe claim**: Seasons are a narrative frame today; the commitment-pooling Cycle gives them their first on-chain form.
- **Evidence**: `docs/docs/reference/glossary-community.md` · `docs/docs/community/where-were-headed.mdx`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Commitment Pool

**Commitment pool** — Gives a garden a shared, honest place for promises — offers and requests curated by the garden, capped per person.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ✗ · in-app ⛔
- **Definition**: A garden-anchored (or protocol root-garden) pool that registers, curates, and reconciles commitments under a charter.
- **Example**: A garden's pool holds an offer to teach a monthly workshop and a request to fix the fence.
- **Also called**: pool (commitment)
- **Not to be confused with Garden**: one pool per garden
- **Not to be confused with Vault**: a pool holds promises, never funds
- **Related**: anchored-to → Garden
- **Safe claim**: Commitment pooling contracts are live and unpaused on Arbitrum with 18 pools registered; the in-app experience is still rolling out.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/interfaces/ICommitmentPoolingModule.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentPoolingModule` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentRegistry` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentPoolingModulePaused` · `.plans/active/commitment-pooling/status.json` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/shared/src/i18n/en.json`

### Commitment Cycle

**Pool cycle** — Bounds a run of promises in time — a Season or a shorter campaign — so reconciliation has a clear close.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ✗ · in-app ⛔
- **Definition**: A bounded run of a pool — a Season or Campaign — seeded with timing and an immutable six-role allocation snapshot at open.
- **Example**: A garden seeds a Season cycle; its commitments reconcile when the cycle closes.
- **Also called**: season cycle · campaign
- **Not to be confused with Season**: the Cycle of type Season is the on-chain representation of the garden's Season
- **Related**: run-of → Commitment Pool
- **Safe claim**: Cycle mechanics are live at the contract layer; no user surface exists yet.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/interfaces/ICommitmentPoolingModule.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentPoolingModule` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentRegistry` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentPoolingModulePaused` · `.plans/active/commitment-pooling/status.json` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/shared/src/i18n/en.json`

### Commitment

**Commitment** — A recorded promise — offer or request — with one accountable lead, evidence, and confirmation by someone other than the doer.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ✗ · in-app ⛔
- **Definition**: A module-native promise record (offer or request) with one accountable lead, an optional contributor roster, repeatable action requirements, direction-aware confirmation, unit accounting in a non-transferable register, and evidence/work linkage — deliberately not an EAS attestation.
- **Example**: “I’ll water the beds while you’re away”, taken up, evidenced with a photo, confirmed by the recipient.
- **Also called**: promise · offer · request
- **Not to be confused with Work**: work documents what happened; the commitment is the promise it fulfills
- **Not to be confused with Attestation**: commitments are module-native records, deliberately not EAS attestations
- **Related**: registered-in → Commitment Pool · optionally-scoped-to → Commitment Cycle · fulfilled-by → Work · optionally-instance-of → Commitment Series · performed-by → Commitment Contributor · optionally-paid-through → Commitment Payout Plan
- **Safe claim**: Commitments are live at the contract layer — a commitment is a record, never a coin: it cannot be traded, sold, or transferred.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/interfaces/ICommitmentPoolingModule.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentPoolingModule` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentRegistry` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentPoolingModulePaused` · `.plans/active/commitment-pooling/status.json` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/shared/src/i18n/en.json`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Commitment Series

**Offer over time** — One durable identity for a repeated offer, so “I teach a workshop each month” is set up once and reused.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ✗ · in-app ⛔
- **Definition**: The internal durable, pool-scoped identity for one Offer used over time. It groups ordinary Offer instances without creating obligations automatically, merging history across pools, or becoming a separate product noun.
- **Example**: A monthly workshop offer paused over the holidays, then resumed.
- **Also called**: standing offer · offer over time
- **Not to be confused with Commitment**: a series is the durable identity; each instance is its own commitment
- **Related**: scoped-to → Commitment Pool · groups-offer-instances → Commitment
- **Safe claim**: Series mechanics are live at the contract layer; the app surface is still rolling out.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/interfaces/ICommitmentPoolingModule.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentPoolingModule` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentRegistry` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentPoolingModulePaused` · `.plans/active/commitment-pooling/status.json` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/shared/src/i18n/en.json`

### Commitment Contributor

**Commitment roster** — Names who helped on a promise; the roster freezes before confirmation so credit can't shift after the fact.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ✓ · indexed ✗ · in-app ⛔
- **Definition**: A person on a commitment's roster whose approved Work or confirmed evidence can earn Hypercert recognition and a contributor payout; one roster member is the accountable lead.
- **Example**: Three gardeners on a fence-repair commitment, frozen at readiness, each credited on fulfillment.
- **Also called**: contributor · roster
- **Not to be confused with gardener**: the roster is the per-commitment team; gardener is the garden-wide role
- **Related**: contributes-to → Commitment · credited-by → Work · recognized-in → Hypercert
- **Safe claim**: Roster and credit-freeze mechanics are live at the contract layer.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/interfaces/ICommitmentPoolingModule.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentPoolingModule` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentRegistry` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → commitmentPoolingModulePaused` · `.plans/active/commitment-pooling/status.json` · `packages/indexer/config.yaml` · `packages/shared/src/i18n/en.json`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Commitment Payout Plan

**Payout plan** — Turns a fulfilled promise into a conserved, hash-bound payment split — every unit accounted for before anything moves.

- **Maturity**: build ✓ · deploy ✓ · active ⛔ · indexed ◐ · in-app ⛔
- **Definition**: A garden-managed split of a fulfilled commitment's declared support into an explicit garden-retained amount and contributor child payouts. Its complete recognition vector is hash-bound, payment weights derive from amounts, and explicit finalization freezes it before dispatch.
- **Example**: A fulfilled campaign commitment finalizes one plan: garden share plus contributor payouts, summing exactly.
- **Also called**: payout plan · settlement plan
- **Not to be confused with Vault**: plans reference value; vaults custody it
- **Related**: pays-for → Commitment · paid-by → Garden · pays → Commitment Contributor
- **Safe claim**: Settlement contracts are deployed but paused; no value moves until the settlement authority activates.
- **Evidence**: `packages/contracts/src/modules/SettlementModule.sol` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → settlementModule` · `packages/contracts/deployments/42161-latest.json → creditRegistry` · `.plans/active/commitment-pooling/status.json` · `packages/indexer/schema.graphql`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15

### Need

**Community need** — Lets a community write down what should change — a problem paired with a desired outcome — so promises and funding can answer it.

- **Maturity**: build ✗ · deploy ✗ · active ✗ · indexed ✗ · in-app ✗
- **Definition**: A community-authored problem statement paired with a mandatory desired outcome, recorded as an immutable EAS attestation whose recipient is the garden. A Need has no request/offer direction — direction belongs to the commitment that answers it.
- **Example**: “The east beds flood every rain; we want working drainage”, later addressed by a fulfilled commitment.
- **Also called**: community need
- **Not to be confused with Commitment**: a Need states the problem; the commitment that answers it carries the offer/request direction
- **Related**: scoped-to → Garden · addressed-by → Commitment
- **Safe claim**: Needs are a planned concept with locked architecture; nothing is deployed or user-visible yet.
- **Evidence**: `.plans/active/community-interface/spec.md`
- **Verified**: 2026-08-15
